title: First plan with a destination: day 1 fully defined, a line on how it progresses, no path
origin: Issue #76 (destination, path and today's step), from the spec's first-plan example

history.text: I log my walks on Strava already
Perfect, Strava it is. Is there something you're working toward with running?

testerLines: Yeah I want to run a mile without stopping by Nov 14. Mon, Wed and Fri work best
whatWentWrong: New case, not a past mistake: before #76 the plan was one step repeated every day, with no destination and no word on how it would progress.
shouldHaveHappened: ZOH shows the plan as a short list: where they're headed (a mile without stopping by Nov 14); day 1's step fully defined (today at 6:30 pm, around their block, easy jog and walk intervals with the minutes and rounds spelled out, about 15 minutes); the usual schedule (Mon, Wed, Fri at 6:30 pm, about 15 minutes); proof as a Strava screenshot. Then a line or two on how it goes from here (how day 1 feels shapes the next runs, building toward the mile), with no list of future steps, and one question. After "love it" it asks for the commitment in natural words; after "I'm in!" it locks with a hype line and when day 1 is.
